actor: Internet exposure measurement researcher, attack-surface scanning organisation
job: Building a fingerprint for unauthenticated Model Context Protocol brokers and running a recurring census of internet-reachable instances.
outcome: A published count of exposed tool brokers, with owner notifications, that responders can later match an intrusion's entry point against.
motivation: Without a measured population and a stable signature, a single compromised broker reads as an anecdote rather than a named access vector.

task.what: Fingerprint exposed Model Context Protocol tool endpoints
task.where: Internet-wide scan infrastructure and exposure dataset pipeline
task.why: A named vector needs a measured exposed population
task.how: Recurring internet-wide port and protocol banner scanning

actor: Detection engineering lead, endpoint and network telemetry vendor
job: Writing detection content that separates a hostile tool invocation from the ordinary broker traffic it is currently indistinguishable from.
outcome: Sensor coverage that records which tool call opened the intrusion, so the entry point survives into the incident write-up.
motivation: Attribution is the binding constraint: a responder who cannot read the broker's own protocol records the outcome and never names the door.

task.who: Detection content and telemetry engineering team
task.what: Ship Model Context Protocol aware detection rules
task.where: Endpoint agent and network sensor detection pipelines
task.why: Unlogged tool calls leave the entry point unnameable
task.how: Protocol parsers plus behavioural rules on tool invocations

actor: Offensive security tooling maintainer, adversary emulation frameworks
job: Adding unauthenticated tool-broker checks to the public scanning frameworks that red teams and opportunistic operators alike run.
outcome: The exposed-broker class becomes commodity coverage in off-the-shelf tooling, so reaching one stops requiring a research-grade effort.
motivation: Coverage parity with published maximum-severity advisories is what these frameworks are judged on, and this class now has several.

task.who: Framework module and scanner template maintainers
task.what: Add unauthenticated tool-broker checks to public frameworks
task.where: Open-source scanner template and emulation module repositories
task.why: Commodity tooling converts a disclosure into routine opportunistic use
task.how: Community-contributed scanner templates against published advisory identifiers

actor: Incident response engagement lead, enterprise security operations
job: Preserving broker request logs and reconstructing the first hostile call whenever a self-hosted agent platform sits inside a breach.
outcome: A forensic timeline that names the tool endpoint as the entry point rather than stopping at the first compromised host.
motivation: Insurers, regulators and the board all ask how they got in, and an unanswered entry point keeps the engagement open.

task.who: Digital forensics and incident response engagement team
task.what: Reconstruct initial access from agent broker request logs
task.where: Breach investigation timelines and log retention configuration
task.why: An unnamed entry point leaves the investigation unresolved
task.how: Broker access logs correlated against host and network telemetry

actor: Threat intelligence research lead, named security vendor publication team
job: Turning a customer breach investigation into a public report whose initial-access section names an internet-reachable, unauthenticated tool endpoint.
outcome: A vendor incident report, not a research advisory, documenting an intrusion whose confirmed initial access was an open tool broker.
motivation: Being first to name a new initial-access vector is the currency these teams publish in, and the case material now exists.

task.who: Threat intelligence research and publication team
task.what: Publish incident report naming open tool endpoint access
task.where: Vendor threat intelligence blog and customer briefings
task.why: First naming of a vector is the publication's value
task.how: Customer investigation data, disclosure review and legal clearance

actor: Known-exploited-vulnerability catalogue analyst, national cyber defence agency
job: Reviewing exploitation evidence for the maximum-severity tool-broker identifiers and adding any that clear the confirmed-in-the-wild bar.
outcome: A catalogue entry for one of these identifiers, which settles the vector's status as firmly as a vendor report would.
motivation: The catalogue exists to force remediation deadlines onto agencies, and it only moves once exploitation is evidenced rather than theorised.

task.who: Vulnerability management and catalogue review analysts
task.what: Evaluate tool-broker identifiers for known-exploited catalogue entry
task.why: A catalogue entry settles the vector on the record
task.how: Confirmed in-the-wild exploitation evidence review criteria
